prov.heading: Provision for Credit Losses
prov.text:
Three - Month Comparison . The Company recorded a provision for credit losses of $680 thousand in the third quarter of 2026, compared to no provision in the prior-year quarter. The increase was primarily related to loan growth, as the loan portfolio increased $146.11 million from the prior-year period, driven largely by the Hometown acquisition completed in the first quarter of 2026.

Nine-Month Comparison . The provision charged to operations increased $1.50 million in the nine months ended September 30, 2026, compared to the same period of 2025. The Company recorded a $1.39 million provision for credit losses on loans and a $150 thousand provision for credit losses on unfunded commitments during the first nine months of 2026, compared to a $58 thousand provision for credit losses on loans and a $22 thousand recovery of provision for credit losses on unfunded loan commitments during the same period in 2025. The increase in total provision expense was primarily driven by growth in the loan portfolio, primarily attributable to loans acquired through the Hometown acquisition.

nonint.heading: Noninterest Expense
nonint.text:
The following table presents the components of, and changes in, noninterest expense for the periods indicated:

Three - Month Comparison . Noninterest expense increased $1.66 million, or 6.32%, in the third quarter of 2026 compared to the same quarter of 2025. The increase was primarily attributable to increases in salaries and employee benefits of $955 thousand, or 6.65%, other operating expense of $471 thousand, or 13.95%, and amortization of intangibles of $401 thousand, or 92.61%.

Nine-Month Comparison . Noninterest expense increased $7.56 million, or 9.86%, in the nine months ended September 30, 2026, compared to the same period of 2025. The increase was primarily attributable to increases of $2.76 million in salaries and employee benefits, $1.52 million in merger expense, and $1.10 million in other operating expense. The merger expense was related to the acquisition of Hometown, which was completed in the first quarter of 2026.

tax.text: The Company’s effective tax rate, income tax as a percent of pre-tax income, may vary significantly from the statutory rate due to permanent differences and available tax credits. Permanent differences are income and expense items excluded by law in the calculation of taxable income. The Company’s most significant permanent differences generally include interest income on municipal securities, increase in the cash surrender value of life insurance policies and non-deductible acquisition costs.

net.heading: Net Income
net.text:
The following table presents the changes in net income and related information for the periods indicated:

Net income for the third quarter of 2026 was $15.42 million, an increase of $3.16 million, or 25.74%, from $12.27 million for the third quarter of 2025. The increase was primarily attributable to higher net interest income and noninterest income. Interest income increased $4.51 million, or 12.62%, driven primarily by a $2.32 million increase in interest and fees on loans and a $1.15 million increase in income from taxable securities. Noninterest income increased $1.76 million, or 16.14%, primarily from a pre-tax gain of $902 thousand from the sale of bank property. These increases were partially offset by a $1.66 million, or 6.32%, increase in noninterest expense, primarily due to higher salaries and employee benefits expense of $955 thousand, increased other operating expense of $471 thousand, and higher amortization of intangible assets of $401 thousand.

Net income for the nine months of 2026, reached a record $49.96 million, surpassing the previous nine-month record of $40.61 million reported in 2021 and increasing $13.63 million compared with the first nine months of 2025.

Net interest income.heading: Net Interest Income
Net interest income.text:
Net interest income, which represents the Company's primary source of earnings, is reviewed by management on both a GAAP basis and a fully taxable equivalent ("FTE") basis (non-GAAP). Management believes presentation of net interest income on an FTE basis enhances comparability of income arising from taxable and tax-exempt sources and is a standard industry measure used by investors, analysts, and banking institutions in evaluating net interest margin, net interest rate spread and operating performance. For additional information, see "Non-GAAP Financial Measures" below.

Noninterest income.heading: Noninterest Income
Noninterest income.text:
The following table presents the components of, and changes in, noninterest income for the periods indicated:

Three - Month Comparison . Noninterest income comprised 26.07% of total net interest and noninterest income in the third quarter of 2026 compared to 25.81% in the same quarter of 2025. Noninterest income increased $1.76 million, or 16.14%, compared to the third quarter of 2025. The increase was primarily attributable to a $902 thousand pre-tax gain on the sale of bank property and growth in other service charges and fees of $565 thousand.

Nine-Month Comparison . Noninterest income comprised 30.86% of total net interest and noninterest income in the nine months ended September 30, 2026, compared to 25.43% in the same period of 2025. Noninterest income increased $14.99 million, or 47.64%, compared to the same period of 2025. The increase was primarily attributable to a $10.38 million pre-tax gain on the sale of the Company's ownership interest in Bearing Insurance, a $1.85 million, or 16.85% growth in other service charges and fees and a $902 thousand pre-tax gain on the sale of bank property.

intro.text: First Community Bankshares, Inc., a financial holding company headquartered in Bluefield, Virginia, provides banking products and services through its wholly owned subsidiary First Community Bank. First Community Bank operated 61 branch banking locations in Virginia, West Virginia, North Carolina, and Tennessee as of June 30, 2026 . First Community Bank offers wealth management and investment advice and services through its Trust Division and through its wholly owned subsidiary, First Community Wealth Management, which collectively managed and administered $ 1.83 billion in combined assets as of June 30, 2026 . The Company reported consolidated assets of $ 3.61 billion as of June 30, 2026 . The Company’s common stock is listed on the NASDAQ Global Select Market under the trading symbol, “FCBC”.
